findings.finding: The plan claims to 'audit ALL existing auto-bug-creation sites and retrofit this same pattern' (USER-REQUIRED ADDITION a; AC#1), but the Scope enumerates only the canary/heartbeat/binding-drift filers (all in scripts/canary_bridge.py) and omits a fourth automated `rebar create bug` site: `_file_conflict_bug_ticket` in the reconciler applier, which files a bug per unresolved (local, Jira) conflict with no dedup tag, no has-tag search, no consecutive-red threshold, and no empty-detail abort.
findings.location: Scope section ('canary/heartbeat/binding-drift filer scripts or workflow logic'); Acceptance Criteria #1; USER-REQUIRED ADDITIONS (a)
scenarios: An unresolved reconciler conflict recurs across many passes, and the filer spams one duplicate bug per pass (the exact duplicate-spam failure mode the plan exists to prevent) because it has no has-tag dedup like canary_bridge.py's _find_alert_ticket
A future create-arg/gate change (0e15/376d class) silently breaks the reconciler conflict filer, and it is never caught because it was excluded from the audit and the contract-doc referencing
findings.suggested_fix: Expand the Scope 'audit table of every auto-file site' to include the reconciler conflict filer, and state whether it gets the full pattern (has-tag dedup on a per-conflict TAG, threshold, templated body with abort-if-empty, detected_by stamp) or is deliberately out of scope with a documented reason.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the durable store for the consecutive-red counter that survives a fresh-runner cron cycle (e.g. a state file committed to the tickets branch, a 'pending' marker ticket/tag, or the Actions run-history API), and specify how the FIRST red is recorded before any alert ticket exists.
evidence: The canary runs on cron `0 * * * *` (.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml) with a fresh ubuntu-latest runner each cycle; the only durable cross-run state is the tickets orphan branch and the alert ticket itself.
On the FIRST red, no alert ticket exists yet (the whole point of the threshold is to NOT file it), so the ticket cannot record the 'one red seen, awaiting a second' pending state.

ABSENCE: the plan's Approach/Scope names no state store (no file on .tickets-tracker, no pending-marker ticket/tag, no derivation from the Actions API run history) where the consecutive-red counter is persisted between runs.
Existing scripts/canary_bridge.py dedup (`_find_alert_ticket`) keys only on an OPEN ticket's presence — it has no notion of prior-run status.
findings.finding: The 'file only after N>=2 consecutive reds' threshold requires durable red/green state across canary cycles, but the plan names no store for it — and in this architecture the first-red marker has nowhere to live.
findings.location: Approach section: 'file only after N>=2 consecutive reds'
scenarios: First red at cycle N stores nothing; cycle N+1 (fresh runner) has no memory of the prior red, so it either files immediately (threshold ineffective) or never crosses the threshold (alert never fires).
findings.suggested_fix: Specify deriving consecutive-red count from the reconcile-bridge run-history the canary already queries (or persist a small JSON marker on the tickets branch), and record the first-red timestamp there; only promote to an alert ticket on the second consecutive red.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify where the per-check dedup state (open-ticket TAG, consecutive-red counter, first-red time, per-day comment marker) lives and how the search-then-create step is made atomic / idempotent against concurrent or re-run workflow invocations (TOCTOU).
evidence: Plan defines shared per-check state (TAG, consecutive-red count, one-comment/day) but no store or ownership is named
'close left to agents' defines retirement but not the counter/day-state lifecycle
has-tag search + conditional create is a check-then-act with no stated atomicity
findings.finding: The dedup/threshold pattern introduces cross-run shared state — a stable per-check TAG (one open ticket per check), a consecutive-red counter (N>=2 gate), a first-red timestamp, and per-day comment accounting — but the plan never says WHERE this state persists or how it is updated atomically. The core 'search has-tag; if none, file' step is a check-then-act sequence with no locking, so two concurrent or re-run workflow invocations can both observe 'no open ticket' and both file, defeating dedup (TOCTOU race).
findings.location: Approach: 'dedup via stable per-check TAG searched with has-tag (one open ticket per check); file only after N>=2 consecutive reds; max one accumulation comment/day'
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor dedup on the tracker's own has-tag query as the single source of truth (idempotent create keyed on TAG), and define counter/day-state persistence (e.g. in the ticket body or a labeled marker) so re-runs and concurrent runs converge on one ticket.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how a green cycle clears any stored first-red/pending state when no alert ticket was ever filed, and confirm the recovery-comment/close path no-ops in that case.
evidence: Current cmd_heartbeat_alert / cmd_binding_drift_alert branch on `stale/drift_found` AND presence of an open ticket; recovery is a transition open->closed that requires a ticket to exist.

With the threshold, a single red followed by green produces NO ticket — fine — but the plan does not state that the recovery/close path must no-op when the first red never crossed the threshold, nor how a stored pending-red marker is cleared on green.
ABSENCE: no statement in Testing/Approach covering the 'first red then green, no ticket ever filed' transition and the clearing of any pending state.
findings.finding: The plan does not reconcile the new 'don't file on first red' threshold with the existing recovery-comment-on-green / auto-close-on-green lifecycle, which today assumes an open ticket exists.
findings.location: Approach section: 'file only after N>=2 consecutive reds' + 'recovery comment on green'
scenarios: Red at cycle N (pending marker set), green at cycle N+1: recovery path must clear the pending marker without a ticket; if unspecified, a stale pending marker could later combine with a fresh red to spuriously cross the threshold.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Cite the detected-by child ticket as an explicit dependency (depends_on / `[rebar:<C>]`) for AC4's REBAR_DETECTED_BY env var.
evidence: 'detected_by stamped by all automated filers (env var from the detected-by child).'

findings.finding: AC4 references a sibling 'detected-by child' ticket (source of REBAR_DETECTED_BY env var) with no cited dependency edge.
scenarios: Filers are retrofitted before REBAR_DETECTED_BY exists, producing tickets without detected_by.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a depends_on edge to the detected-by child and reference it as `REBAR_DETECTED_BY [rebar:<child-id>]` in the plan.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the dedup search+create stays idempotent under concurrent filer runs (e.g. tag-uniqueness re-check, single-run gate, or create-then-dedup-collapse).
evidence: 'dedup via stable per-check TAG searched with has-tag (one open ticket per check)'
No mention of idempotency/locking/atomicity between the dedup search and the create call.
findings.finding: The dedup mechanism (has-tag search, then create-if-none) is a check-then-act sequence with no stated protection against a race between two concurrent filer runs both finding no open ticket and both filing.
findings.location: Approach — 'dedup via stable per-check TAG searched with has-tag (one open ticket per check)'
scenarios: Two workflow runs (retry, or two failing checks) execute concurrently and both create a ticket for the same check, defeating the one-open-ticket invariant.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how filers surface (log/alert/exit-code) a failed dedup search or failed rebar create, and add a unit test for the create-failure path.
evidence: Filers invoke rebar create and a has-tag search (external/CLI calls) but only the empty-detail case has an 'abort with loud log' behavior; other failure modes are unspecified.
Testing section covers red/green/comment/empty-detail but not create-command failure.
findings.finding: The plan does not specify error handling for the filer's own external operations (dedup has-tag search failure, rebar create failure) or surface those failures.
scenarios: rebar create returns non-zero (gate change, auth failure) — the 0e15/376d class the plan cites — and the filer silently no-ops.

findings.finding: The unit-test list covers the single-filer state machine (first/second/third red, green, empty-detail) but does not test the dedup boundary that matters most: a has-tag search that FINDS an existing open ticket (so no duplicate is filed) and the concurrent/re-run case where two invocations race the search-then-create step.
findings.location: Testing section and AC 'Filer behavior covered by the unit tests above.'
